_comment: Vulnerable / end-of-life software rules used by aegis/scanners/software.py.
Fields: id, name_regex (case-insensitive, searched in the installed program's display name),
severity (info|low|medium|high|critical), advice (plain-English action), cve (string or list, optional),
max_vulnerable_version: affected when installed version <= this value (inclusive)
fixed_version:          affected when installed version <  this value (exclusive)
exact_versions: [..]    affected only for these exact versions
Optional: exclude_regex (skip names matching), version_from_name (regex with one group; used instead of
DisplayVersion, e.g. Java 'Update 361'), eol (true => reported as unsupported software), eol_date (YYYY-MM-DD;
rule only applies on/after this date), platforms (default [windows, darwin]; Linux distro packages
backport fixes so version-based rules are unreliable there), title (finding title override), reference (URL/ID).

rules.advice: Adobe Flash Player has been dead since December 2020 and is full of unpatched, actively exploited holes. Uninstall it (Adobe's official uninstaller is at helpx.adobe.com/flash-player/kb/uninstall-flash-player-windows.html).
Adobe Shockwave Player was discontinued in April 2019 and has unpatched vulnerabilities. Uninstall it.
Microsoft Silverlight reached end of support on 2021-10-12 and no longer gets security fixes. Uninstall it unless a legacy application you still need requires it.

rules.cve: multiple (Apple ended QuickTime for Windows support in 2016; CISA/US-CERT alert TA16-105A)
rules.advice: Apple stopped patching QuickTime for Windows in 2016 and known flaws can never be fixed. Uninstall it (Settings > Apps) - modern players such as VLC handle the same media files.

rules.cve: multiple (Java 6 and 7 are long past end of public updates)
rules.advice: Java 6 and 7 have not received public security updates for years and are a favourite exploit-kit target. Uninstall them; if an application needs Java, install a current supported version (Java 17/21 LTS, for example Eclipse Temurin).

This Java 8 build is missing at least two years of security fixes. Update Java (java.com or your vendor's installer) to the latest Java 8 update, or move to a current LTS release such as Java 17 or 21.

WinRAR before 7.13 has a path-traversal flaw (CVE-2025-8088) that was exploited in the wild by the RomCom group: opening a booby-trapped archive can silently drop malware into your Startup folder. Update WinRAR to 7.13 or newer from rarlab.com.
7-Zip before 24.09 lets archives bypass Windows' 'Mark of the Web' protection (CVE-2025-0411), so downloaded malware runs without SmartScreen warnings. Update to 24.09 or newer from 7-zip.org.
Python 2 has been unsupported since 1 January 2020 and receives no security fixes. Migrate scripts to Python 3 and uninstall Python 2.

PuTTY before 0.81 leaks private-key bits when you use NIST P-521 ECDSA keys (CVE-2024-31497, enough for an attacker to recover the key) and earlier versions are exposed to the Terrapin attack. Update PuTTY from chiark.greenend.org.uk/~sgtatham/putty/ and replace any P-521 keys.
Notepad++ before 8.8.2 has an installer privilege-escalation flaw (CVE-2025-49144). Update from notepad-plus-plus.org.
VLC before 3.0.21 can be crashed or exploited with a malformed media file (CVE-2024-46461 and others). Update VLC from videolan.org.

rules.cve: multiple (end of life: Reader X 2015, XI 2017)
rules.advice: This version of Adobe Acrobat/Reader is long out of support and has many unpatched, exploited PDF vulnerabilities. Uninstall it and install the current Adobe Acrobat Reader (or use your browser's built-in PDF viewer).
This Adobe Acrobat release is out of support and no longer receives security patches. Upgrade to the current Acrobat or Acrobat Reader.
Microsoft Office 2010 stopped receiving security updates on 2020-10-13; Word/Excel exploits for it stay open forever. Upgrade to Microsoft 365 or a supported Office version.
Microsoft Office 2013 stopped receiving security updates on 2023-04-11. Upgrade to Microsoft 365 or a supported Office version.

Microsoft Office 2016 and 2019 stopped receiving security updates on 2025-10-14. Upgrade to Microsoft 365, Office 2024 or another supported version; until then keep macros disabled and avoid opening unexpected attachments.
Microsoft Office 2021 reached end of support on 2026-10-13. Upgrade to Microsoft 365 or Office 2024.
Internet Explorer was retired on 2022-06-15 and receives no security updates. Use Microsoft Edge (which has an IE-compatibility mode if a legacy site demands it).
This Zoom client is more than a year behind and misses many security fixes (see zoom.com/trust/security-bulletin). Update from Zoom's menu: profile picture > Check for updates.

rules.title: Outdated web browser: Google Chrome
rules.advice: This Google Chrome is two or more years out of date and missing dozens of exploited-in-the-wild fixes. Open chrome://settings/help to update, then restart Chrome.

rules.title: Outdated web browser: Microsoft Edge
rules.advice: This Microsoft Edge is two or more years out of date. Open edge://settings/help to update, then restart Edge.

rules.title: Outdated web browser: Mozilla Firefox
rules.advice: This Firefox is older than the current Extended Support Release (128) and no longer receives security updates. Open Menu > Help > About Firefox to update.

rules.cve: OpenSSL 1.1.1 and older are end of life (1.1.1: 2023-09-11)
rules.advice: OpenSSL 1.x no longer receives public security fixes. Update to OpenSSL 3.x (or uninstall it if no program of yours needs it).

TeamViewer before 15.8.3 has an unquoted URI handler flaw (CVE-2020-13699) that lets a web page steal your TeamViewer session credentials, and old versions are also a favourite of tech-support scammers. Update TeamViewer or uninstall it if you do not use it.
This exact CCleaner build (5.33.6162 / Cloud 1.07.3191) shipped with the Floxif backdoor. Uninstall it, update to a current CCleaner (or remove it) and run a full antivirus scan.
